title: Conduct of the Informal Conference and the Board Hearing — Decision Reviews and Appeals
content:
# Practice note: the informal conference and the Board hearing

**Scope.** This note covers the two oral proceedings in Decision Reviews and Appeals: the telephone informal conference in a Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference, and the hearing on a Board Appeal - Hearing Docket.

## Rule

A Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference includes one telephone conference in which the claimant or representative may point out specific errors but may not present new evidence. A Hearing Docket appeal includes one hearing of the requested type before a Veterans Law Judge, which can be rescheduled 1 time for good cause; a transcript is added to the record. Hearings are scheduled in docket order with advanced appeals first.

## The informal conference

- Lane: Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference only; the other five lanes hold 0 conferences.
- Number: one conference per request.
- Form: by telephone, with the senior reviewer.
- Who speaks: the claimant or the representative.
- Content: specific errors may be pointed out; new evidence may not be presented.
- Record: the conference is recorded on the review with its date.

## The Board hearing

- Lane: Board Appeal - Hearing Docket only.
- Number: one hearing, of the type requested — a virtual tele-hearing, a videoconference hearing or a central office hearing.
- Decision-maker: a Veterans Law Judge.
- Rescheduling: the scheduled hearing can be rescheduled 1 time for good cause.
- Transcript: a transcript of the hearing is added to the record.
- Record: the hearing is recorded on the appeal with its date and the hearing type held.

## Scheduling order — a worked example (hypothetical)

Three Hearing Docket appeals are waiting, in docket order: appeal A first, appeal B second, appeal C third. Appeal B has been advanced on the docket; A and C have not. Hearings are scheduled in docket order with advanced appeals first, so the order is B, then A, then C.

## Points of judgement

**Hypothetical: a claimant in a Higher-Level Review with Informal Conference wishes to read a new medical opinion into the conference.** New evidence may not be presented in the conference; the claimant or representative may point out specific errors.

**Hypothetical: a Hearing Docket hearing has been rescheduled once for good cause and the appellant asks for a second reschedule.** The hearing can be rescheduled 1 time for good cause, and that one reschedule has been used.

**Who may take part in the informal conference on the claimant's side?** The claimant or the representative.
